rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: in a deflection, the defender left its post and the piece it guarded fell. In an attraction, you give up a piece to pull the king to a square where the blow lands on it.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.e2: This position comes from a game played on Lichess, and White is to move. The black rook on f8 guards the eighth rank, and your rook on d7 watches e7 and f7.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.p: Find the piece you can give up to pull the black king to a square where it gets mated.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.certo: The queen captures the rook on f8 with check. The king has to capture it, and on f8 it stands on the rank your rook on b2 can reach.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is the queen to f8, capturing the rook with check: the king has to capture it, and on f8 your rook on b2 awaits it on the eighth rank.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.err.c5e7.1: The queen goes to e7, but it forces nothing: the rook on f8 still guards the eighth rank.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.err.c5e7.2: With this move, Black has a resource: the queen gives check on h3, backed by the bishop on g4, and keeps checking your king.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.err.c5e7.3: Back to the position: look for the check that gives up a piece and forces the black king to capture.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.err.c5a7.1: The queen captures the pawn on a7, but it forces nothing: the rook on f8 still guards the eighth rank.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.err.c5a7.2: With this move, Black has a resource: the queen gives check on h3, backed by the bishop on g4, and keeps checking your king.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.err.c5a7.3: Back to the position: look for the check that gives up a piece and forces the black king to capture.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.err.b2b7.1: The rook doubles on the seventh rank, but it forces nothing: the rook on f8 still guards the eighth.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.err.b2b7.2: With this move, Black has a resource: the queen gives check on h3, backed by the bishop on g4, and keeps checking your king.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.err.b2b7.3: Back to the position: look for the check that gives up a piece and forces the black king to capture.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not force the black king off g8. Look for a check that gives up a piece.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: look for the check that gives up a piece and forces the black king to capture.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.l1: The king has no good way out. On h7, the queen would capture on g7 with mate, defended by the rook on d7. So it captures the queen.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.l2: On f8 the king can only move along the eighth rank: e7 and f7 belong to your rook on d7, and g7 holds its own pawn.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.l3: The rook gives check on b8, and it is mate. The queen you gave up pulled the king to the square where the blow awaited it.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex1.l4: In positions like this, before giving up the piece, look at the square the king goes to and check that the next blow is ready.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: White again, and now the attraction wins material. Your queen and the rook on f7 attack each other, only the king defends the rook, and the black queen is far away, on h3.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.p: Find the piece you can give up to pull the black king to a square where a fork awaits it.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.certo: The queen captures the rook on f7 with check. If the king captures it, it goes to f7, and the knight on g5 attacks the king and the queen on h3 at the same time.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.revela: The move is the queen to f7, capturing the rook with check: on f7 the king is within reach of the knight, which goes to g5 with check and attacks the queen on h3.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.err.e7d6.1: The queen captures the pawn on d6 and escapes the rook, but your king stays exposed to the queen on h3.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.err.e7d6.2: With this move, Black has a resource: the queen captures on g3 with check, backed by the pawn on f4, and the attack on your king decides.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.err.e7d6.3: Back to the position: look for the check that gives up a piece and brings the black king near your knight.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.err.e7g5.1: The queen goes to g5 and attacks the pawn on g6, but it forces nothing.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.err.e7g5.2: With this move, Black has a resource: the pawn captures on g3 with check and opens the f-file for the rook on f7, which now attacks your knight.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.err.e7g5.3: Back to the position: look for the check that gives up a piece and brings the black king near your knight.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.err.f3g5.1: The knight attacks the queen on h3, but it leaves your queen on e7 attacked by the rook on f7.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.err.f3g5.2: With this move, Black has a resource: the queen escapes with check on h2, and then the rook captures your queen on e7.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.err.f3g5.3: Back to the position: look for the check that gives up a piece and brings the black king near your knight.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not pull the black king to the fork square. Look for a check that gives up a piece.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: look for the check that gives up a piece and brings the black king near your knight.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.l1: On h6 or h8 the king would leave your queen alive on f7, and Black would lose even more. So it captures the queen.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.l2: The king captures the queen and goes to f7. It is a square the knight reaches from g5, where it also attacks the queen on h3.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.l3: The knight gives check on g5 and attacks the queen on h3: it is a fork. The pawn on h4 defends the knight, and the king cannot capture it.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.l4: The king steps out of check, and the queen on h3 is left undefended.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.l5: The knight captures the queen. White gave the queen for a rook and won the black queen: White comes out a rook up.
rot.attraction.ideia.ex2.l6: In positions like this, an attraction also wins material: the square the king goes to can be the square of a fork.
rot.attraction.demos.partida.1: Attack: White again, in a game played on Lichess. The bishop on f8 closes the eighth rank in front of the king, and your rooks are doubled on the d-file.
rot.attraction.demos.partida.2: The rook captures the bishop with check. The king has no other square: h8 is still on the rook's line, and h7, f7 and g7 hold black pieces.
rot.attraction.demos.partida.3: The king captures the rook and goes to f8. The squares e7, f7 and g7 hold black pieces, and the king can only move along the eighth rank.
rot.attraction.demos.partida.4: The other rook gives check on d8, and it is mate. The rook you gave up pulled the king to f8, where it was trapped.
rot.attraction.demos.pretas.1: Attack: now with Black. The white bishop on f1 shields the king, and your rook on d6 can reach the first rank.
rot.attraction.demos.pretas.2: The queen captures the bishop with check. On h2 the king would be mated by the queen on g2, backed by the bishop on f3. So it captures.
rot.attraction.demos.pretas.3: On f1 the king has no square: your bishop on f3 watches e2 and g2, and the white pawn on f2 blocks f2.
rot.attraction.demos.pretas.4: The rook gives check on d1, and it is mate. Once again, the piece given up led the king to the square where the blow awaited it.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.1: Attack: White again. Your queen on h6 and the pawn on f6 hem in the black king. A queen given up with check can pull it, but first see which black piece will capture it.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.p: Find the piece to give up that forces the king, and no other piece, to capture.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.certo: The queen captures the pawn on h7 with check. Only the king can capture it: the rook on g8 does not reach h7.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.revela: The move is the queen to h7: only the king reaches that square, and on h7 it stands on the h-file, which your rook on f4 can reach.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.err.h6g7.1: The queen gives check on g7, but the rook on g8 also reaches g7.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.err.h6g7.2: With this move, Black has a resource: the rook on g8 captures the queen, and the king stays on h8, far from any blow.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.err.h6g7.3: Back to the position: look for the square where only the king can capture your queen.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.err.f4h4.1: The rook goes to the h-file and threatens mate on h7, but it gives Black time.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.err.f4h4.2: With this move, Black has a resource: the queen gives check on d5 and starts a series of checks on your king.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.err.f4h4.3: Back to the position: look for the square where only the king can capture your queen.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.err.f4e4.1: The rook goes to e4 and threatens to enter the eighth rank, but it stands on your king's diagonal.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.err.f4e4.2: With this move, Black has a resource: the queen goes to d5 and attacks the rook on e4, which cannot step out from in front of your king.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.err.f4e4.3: Back to the position: look for the square where only the king can capture your queen.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.2: The king has no other square: g7 is watched by the queen and by the pawn on f6. So it captures the queen.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.2b: The king captures and goes to h7, on the h-file.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.3: The rook gives check on h4, and it is mate: g6 and g8 hold black pieces, the pawn on f6 watches g7, and h6 and h8 are on the rook's file.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.4: In positions like this, before giving up the piece, check which enemy piece will capture it.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.s1: Compare with the queen on g7, which also gives check.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.s2: On g7 the queen can also be reached by the rook on g8.
rot.attraction.demos.excecao.s3: The rook is the one that captures, and the king stays safe on h8. The queen is lost.
rot.attraction.pratica.valeAqui.err2.g5g: The queen captures the rook on g8, but the rook on b8 recaptures it, and the attack is over. On h7 the king stands on the h-file: look for the mate.
rot.attraction.pratica.valeAqui.enunciad: Now you play. Before giving up a piece, see who will capture it. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.attraction.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The rook captured the queen on h7 with check, and the king had to capture the rook. On h7 it stood on the h-file, and the other rook gave mate on h2.
rot.attraction.pratica.valeAqui.err.g5g8: The queen captures the rook on g8 with check, but the rook on b8 recaptures, not the king. You give up the queen, and the king stays on h8. Look for the move that forces the king itself to capture.
rot.attraction.pratica.valeAqui.err.f2h2: The rook doubles on the h-file, but the rook on g8 captures your queen on g5 with check, and your attack is over. Look for the move that forces the king to capture.
rot.attraction.pratica.torre.enunciado: White again. Before you move, see where the king can be pulled. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.attraction.pratica.torre.fim: The rook captured the pawn on h7 with check, and the king had to capture it. On h7 the queen gave mate on h5: your bishop on d5 watches g8.
rot.attraction.pratica.torre.err.d1h5: The queen goes to h5 and threatens to capture on h7, but Black advances the pawn to h6 and holds. Look for the piece to give up that pulls the king to h7 now.
rot.attraction.pratica.torre.err.h4h3: The rook leaves the h-file, and the black king faces no threat. Look for the piece to give up that pulls the king to h7.
rot.attraction.pratica.peao.err2.g5g4: The pawn gives check on g4, but the king goes back to g2 and escapes the net. On h3 it has no free square: look for the mate.
rot.attraction.pratica.peao.err2.a1g7: The queen retreats, and the white king escapes. On h3 it has no free square: look for the mate.
rot.attraction.pratica.peao.enunciado: Now with Black. The white king is on g2, hemmed in by its own pawns. Before you move, see where it can be pulled. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.attraction.pratica.peao.fim: The pawn gave check on h3, and the king had to capture it. On h3 it had no square left, and the queen gave mate on f1.
rot.attraction.pratica.peao.err.a1g7: The queen goes back to defend your king, and White stays a rook up. Look for a check that pulls the white king to a square with no way out.
rot.attraction.pratica.peao.err.h4g3: The pawn captures on g3, but without check: White gains time to attack your king. Look for the check that pulls the white king to a square with no way out.
rot.attraction.pratica.garfo.err2.g5h7: The knight captures the pawn with check, but it does not attack the rook on d4. Look for the check that attacks the king and the rook at the same time.
rot.attraction.pratica.garfo.err3.e6d8: The knight runs away, but the rook on d4 is still alive. Capture the piece the fork attacked.
rot.attraction.pratica.garfo.enunciado: White again. The black rook on d4 is far from its king. Before you move, see where the king can be pulled. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.attraction.pratica.garfo.fim: The rook captured the rook on f8 with check, and the king had to capture it. On f8 the knight gave check on e6 and attacked the rook on d4 at the same time, then captured it.
rot.attraction.pratica.garfo.err.g5e6: The knight attacks the rook on d4, but without check: Black checks on b4 and then captures your rook on f1. Look for the piece to give up that pulls the king to the fork square.
rot.attraction.pratica.garfo.err.f1h1: The rook leaves the f-file, and Black gains time: the rook on d4 checks on b4. Look for the piece to give up that pulls the king to the fork square.
